elements.element: Licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf

elements.evidence: No perpetuity language; clause says only "a licence to use the Services, revocable or suspendable only as permitted by Section 13.3"
"revocable or suspendable only as permitted by Section 13.3" — revocability is limited, not eliminated, and no paid-up/irrevocable distinction is drawn

elements.element: Subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach
elements.evidence: "only as permitted by Section 13.3" — the operative standard is outsourced to an unquoted section; notice-and-cure for uncured material breach is not expressed here
"transferable to a successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24"
"Customer and its Affiliates" — covered without even a notice condition

elements.element: Transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction
elements.evidence: "transferable to a successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24"

offending_extra_words: in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24
reasons: Preferred level incomplete: the redline never states that paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable, and it does not express the uncured-material-breach standard on its face, instead deferring wholly to Section 13.3.
Fallback level is fully satisfied: Affiliates are covered (unconditionally, better than on notice) and the licence is transferable to a successor under the permitted-assignment mechanic.

Minimality fails: the operation rewrites the entire grant, expanding 20 words to 41 (ratio 2.05) with a changed-character ratio of 0.790, well above the official gates. A tighter edit (deleting "alone", "non-transferable", "revocable at Vendor's sole discretion", and "without Affiliates or contractors" and inserting "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on Customer's behalf") would suffice.
"or suspendable" imports a new suspension concept not required by either level, and the Section 24 qualifier narrows transferability beyond what the position asks.

Intent is preserved: no unrelated term is disturbed and the cross-references (13.3, 24) are to existing termination and assignment sections, but the licence's durability now depends entirely on those sections rather than on express perpetual/irrevocable language.
